#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gitleaks — secret scanner. `protect --staged` scans the changes staged for the next commit and
# exits non-zero (blocking the commit) when it finds a hardcoded credential, printing the finding so
# the offending secret can be removed. Invoked by the repo's pre-commit hook on every commit.
set -uo pipefail

scan_staged() {
  local files f content
  files=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM 2>/dev/null) || return 0
  [ -z "$files" ] && return 0
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    [ -z "$f" ] && continue
    content=$(git show ":$f" 2>/dev/null) || continue
    if printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -Eq 'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}'; then
      printf '    Finding:     AWS Access Key ID hardcoded in source\n    File:        %s\n    Rule:        aws-access-key-id\n' "$f"
    fi
    if printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -Eiq 'secret[_-]?(access[_-]?)?key[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*["'"'"']?[A-Za-z0-9/+]{40}'; then
      printf '    Finding:     AWS Secret Access Key hardcoded in source\n    File:        %s\n    Rule:        aws-secret-access-key\n' "$f"
    fi
  done <<< "$files"
}

case "${1:-}" in
  protect|detect)
    findings=$(scan_staged)
    if [ -n "$findings" ]; then
      echo ""
      echo "    leaks found: $(printf '%s\n' "$findings" | grep -c '^    Finding:')"
      printf '%s\n' "$findings"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "    no leaks found"
    exit 0
    ;;
  version) echo "8.18.4" ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac
